Who we serve

Reusable tasting glassware and tasting room tools for wineries

Tasting rooms need glassware that presents the wine properly, survives a stone terrace, and carries the estate's name. We supply the ISO-profile tasting glass, the pourers, the stoppers and the spittoon buckets as one order.

Request a quoteBrowse the catalogue

What usually goes wrong

The five problems we hear most from this buyer type.

  • Breakage on terraces, lawns and vineyard tours
  • Glasses that cannot go into an estate-branded gift programme
  • Spittoons that look improvised and unhygienic
  • Pourers that drip and stoppers that leak
  • Guest take-home glasses that have to be worth keeping

Present the wine properly, then survive the terrace

The ISO-profile tasting glass in our range is moulded in Tritan at 220 ml with the tulip bowl and tapered rim that keep aromatics focused, so it presents a flight the way a judging room would recognise. Because it is moulded rather than blown, it goes onto a stone terrace, into a tour group's hands and through a commercial wash cycle without becoming a liability.

For guided tastings, the standard stemmed wine glass in PS or acrylic covers the volume seating where the estate's own glass would be at risk, at a replacement cost that does not affect the tasting fee margin.

The unglamorous items that make a tasting room work

A tasting room is judged on the whole table, and the pourers, stoppers and spittoons are part of it. Our vacuum stoppers preserve an open bottle for up to seven days and the date-scale versions let a host mark when the bottle was opened. The wine tasting spittoon buckets are purpose-built for guided flights — hygienic, stackable and available in a mini size for individual place settings.

If your gift shop sells a stopper or a pourer at the counter, the same order can carry an estate-branded version with a logo printed or moulded onto it, which turns a functional item into a memento.

Estate branding and gift programmes

Estate-branded glassware is the most-used item a visitor takes home. Pad printing, laser engraving and electroplating are available, along with custom colour matching so the glass carries the estate's palette. Retail colour boxes and UPC barcodes make the same item ready for a shelf or an online store without a separate packaging project.

Reusable tasting glassware and tasting room tools for wineries — questions

Do you supply an ISO-profile tasting glass?

Yes. Model PG8900 is a 220 ml ISO-standard wine tasting glass moulded in Tritan, 53 g in weight, available with an estate logo.

What is the best spittoon for a tasting room?

Model IB200 is a 3.7 L purpose-built wine tasting spittoon bucket, and model IB201 is a 700 ml mini version for individual place settings.

Do your stoppers work on open bottles?

The vacuum stopper range (SP-016, SP-002-A and SP-002S) is designed to preserve an open bottle, with date-scale versions for tracking when the bottle was opened. The champagne stopper range is designed for sparkling wine under pressure.

Which drinkware and accessories suit a tasting room?

The range covers tasting and serving drinkware, pourers and stoppers, vacuum preservation accessories and spittoon buckets. Select the SKUs that match the serve you pour and submit the list with the quantity per item.

Wine stoppers and pourers · Ice buckets and coolers

What should a winery provide for a branded tasting-glass quote?

Provide the SKU, the quantity, the logo artwork, the intended logo position, the packaging configuration and the destination. If the glass doubles as retail merchandise, state the retail packaging requirement as well.

Request a quote

Can a winery combine drinkware, openers, stoppers and packaging in one project?

Yes. A combined project is quoted as one build with the items, the packaging configuration and the quantities confirmed together, and consolidated into a single shipment.

Gift box packaging guide

How should a winery plan a replenishment order?

Plan the replenishment from the annual pour volume and the breakage allowance rather than from the shelf count. Send the annual volume and the number of deliveries you want so the quantities and the packing are quoted for that schedule.

Wholesale programme

What product data should be retained for repeat orders?

Keep the SKU, the mould record, the material, the decoration method, the Pantone reference, the packing configuration and the approved pre-production sample. Those records are what make a reorder reproducible.
